name: JEV-35B
context_scaling: Inherited from Qwen3.5-35B-A3B; the card does not claim an extended context and serves short decision requests (median latency in milliseconds).
attention_variant: Inherited unchanged from Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 10 full GQA layers (kv heads 2, head_dim 256) with 30 gated linear-attention layers. Serving shape is unusual rather than the architecture: a classification head over supplied options (yes/no, 0-5 score, or choice) via POST /v1/decide.
notes: ADDED 2026-10-21. A decision/classification post-train of Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: instead of free-form generation it returns a probability over the options you hand it, with an optional second reasoning pass when System 1 is unsure. That makes it a different tool, not a better chat model, and it is recorded because 648K downloads says people are using it as a judge/guardrail. Its own table compares to JEV-27B-VL, not to the Qwen base, so this record carries ABSOLUTE scores only — there is no published base delta and none should be inferred. Absolute numbers are unremarkable for the size (GPQA Diamond 36.0, MMLU-Pro 64.2) and GSM8K 36.0 is well below its own 27B-VL sibling at 54.2, which the card does not explain. The credible part is the operational claim: all 140,178 scoreable requests answered with zero errors, and its latency advantage in single-pass mode.
